reference_use.conclusion: Snapshot: project 63436ae6 + Mathlib 25730c7c. The snapshot Contract.lean is byte-identical to the workspace Contract.lean and Submission.lean. SimonGMT Chapter08/VarifoldConvergence.lean already proves RadonConverges.firstVariation_tendsto, firstVariationNormOn_le_liminf, hasLocallyBoundedFirstVariation and firstVariationRieszMeasure_le_liminf. FirstVariationRiesz.lean:218 firstVariationRieszMeasure_eq_norm identifies variationMeasure with firstVariationNormOn on W ⊂⊂ U. Remark 3.8(1) (child variation_lsc) therefore needs no sibling. The VarifoldConvergence module states that it does not prove the lower-density part. SimonGMT has no portmanteau for varifold weights: the only *_le_liminf lemmas are for first variation, BV and currents (Chapter06/Mass.lean WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf), hence the child weight_portmanteau. Mathlib supplies the needed tools: Besicovitch covering families (Covering/Besicovitch.lean:455 exist_disjoint_covering_families, whose BallPackage needs only bounded radii; HasBesicovitchCovering is inferred for Euclidean N); countability of disjoint balls (Topology/Bases.lean:493); Urysohn (UrysohnsLemma.lean:404, LocallyCompact.lean:172); and the thickening and ℝ≥0∞ liminf lemmas. ENNReal.liminf_const_mul does not exist, so the proofs use Monotone.map_liminf_of_continuousAt. All 6 child lean_statements pass validate_lean_statement and elaborate in the replayed contract scope. subproblem.title: Mass lower bounds at nearby points pass to the Radon limit and force lower density ≥ 1
subproblem.statement: Let V_i (i ∈ ℕ) and V be n-varifolds on U ⊆ ℝ^N with V_i → V as Radon measures on G_n(U) (Varifold.RadonConverges Vi V). Let x ∈ ℝ^N, ρ₀ > 0 with B°_{ρ₀}(x) ⊆ U, Λ ∈ ℝ, q : ℕ → ℕ with q_i → ∞, and y : ℕ → ℝ^N with y_i → x. Suppose e^{-Λρ}·ω_n·ρ^n ≤ μ_{V_{q_i}}(B_ρ(y_i)) for every i and every 0 < ρ < ρ₀. Then e^{-Λρ}·ω_n·ρ^n ≤ μ_V(B_ρ(x)) for every 0 < ρ < ρ₀, and liminf_{ρ↓0} μ_V(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρ^n) ≥ 1 (the liminf of densityRatio n μ_V x along 𝓝[>] 0).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (Vi : ℕ → Varifold N n U) (V : Varifold N n U) (x : Euclidean N) (ρ₀ Λ : ℝ) (q : ℕ → ℕ) (y : ℕ → Euclidean N), Varifold.RadonConverges Vi V → 0 < ρ₀ → ball x ρ₀ ⊆ U → Tendsto q atTop atTop → Tendsto y atTop (𝓝 x) → (∀ i, ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ < ρ₀ → ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (-(Λ * ρ))) * unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal ρ ^ n ≤ (Vi (q i)).weight (closedBall (y i) ρ)) → (∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ < ρ₀ → ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (-(Λ * ρ))) * unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal ρ ^ n ≤ V.weight (closedBall x ρ)) ∧ 1 ≤ liminf (densityRatio n V.weight x) (𝓝[>] 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the second half of printed step (4) of the proof of 3.7 (“Fix 0 < ρ < ρ0; for i large, |y_i − x| < ρ and B_{ρ−|y_i−x|}(y_i) ⊆ B_ρ(x), so by (P2) μ(B_ρ(x)) ≥ limsup_i μ_{q_i}(B_ρ(x)) ≥ limsup_i e^{-jρ}ω_n(ρ − |y_i − x|)^n = e^{-jρ} ω_n ρ^n. Hence the lower density … ≥ 1”), stated for general Λ, q and y.

Notation: μ = V.weight, μ_j = (V_j).weight, ω_n = unitBallVolume n, and F(r) := ofReal(e^{-Λr}) · ω_n · ofReal(r)^n ∈ [0,∞) for r ∈ ℝ.

1. ω_n ∈ (0,∞): it is the Lebesgue measure of the open unit ball of ℝ^n (Metric.measure_ball_pos, measure_ball_lt_top). F is continuous from ℝ to [0,∞]: r ↦ ofReal(e^{-Λr})·ω_n and r ↦ ofReal(r)^n are continuous with finite values, and multiplication on [0,∞] is continuous at every pair of finite values (ENNReal.Tendsto.mul with the side conditions “≠ ∞”).

2. Mass bound for V. Fix ρ with 0 < ρ < ρ₀ and put K := B_ρ(x) (closed ball). K is compact and K ⊆ B°_{ρ₀}(x) ⊆ U, so by (P2) of the sibling weight_portmanteau_of_radonConverges, limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K).
 Let d_i := dist(y_i, x) → 0 and r_i := ρ − d_i. Then r_i → ρ and, by continuity, F(r_i) → F(ρ).
 For every i with d_i < ρ (which holds for all large i): 0 < r_i ≤ ρ < ρ₀, and B_{r_i}(y_i) ⊆ K, since dist(z, y_i) ≤ r_i implies dist(z, x) ≤ r_i + d_i = ρ. By hypothesis, F(r_i) ≤ μ_{q_i}(B_{r_i}(y_i)) ≤ μ_{q_i}(K).
 Therefore F(ρ) = limsup_i F(r_i) ≤ limsup_i μ_{q_i}(K) ≤ limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K).
 - The first inequality holds because F(r_i) ≤ μ_{q_i}(K) eventually.
 - The second holds because q_i → ∞: with f(j) = μ_j(K), limsup_i f(q_i) is the limsup of f along the image filter map q atTop (Filter.limsup_comp), and map q atTop ≤ atTop, so it is ≤ limsup_j f(j) (Filter.limsup_le_limsup_of_le).
 This is the first conclusion.

3. Lower density. For 0 < ρ < ρ₀ the denominator D(ρ) := ω_n·ofReal(ρ)^n lies in (0,∞), so step 2 gives ofReal(e^{-Λρ}) ≤ μ(B_ρ(x))/D(ρ) = densityRatio n μ x ρ (ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le). Since Ioo 0 ρ₀ ∈ 𝓝[>] 0, densityRatio n μ x ≥ ofReal(e^{-Λ·}) eventually along 𝓝[>] 0. Also ofReal(e^{-Λr}) → ofReal(e^0) = 1 as r → 0, by continuity. Hence 1 = liminf_{r↓0} ofReal(e^{-Λr}) ≤ liminf_{r↓0} densityRatio n μ x r (Tendsto.liminf_eq and liminf_le_liminf; in the complete lattice [0,∞] no boundedness side conditions are needed). This is the second conclusion. ∎
proof_key_steps: F(r) = e^{-Λr} ω_n r^n is continuous with finite values; ω_n ∈ (0,∞).
For fixed ρ < ρ₀ and large i, B_{ρ−d_i}(y_i) ⊆ B_ρ(x) =: K, so F(ρ − d_i) ≤ μ_{q_i}(K).
F(ρ) = lim F(ρ − d_i) ≤ limsup μ_{q_i}(K) ≤ limsup μ_j(K) ≤ μ_V(K), by q_i → ∞ and portmanteau (P2).
Dividing by ω_n ρ^n: densityRatio ≥ e^{-Λρ} on (0, ρ₀), whose limit at 0⁺ is 1, so the lower density is ≥ 1.

audit.reason: Shrinking radii give eventual ball inclusion, and q tending to infinity suffices for the subsequence limsup inequality. Compact-set portmanteau and continuity transfer the mass bound; division and the exponential limit prove lower density at least one. The proof supports arbitrary real Λ as stated.
